messages:
Maria Chen: Hey team — I'm starting today and trying to get kubectl access. I need access to namespace team-platform-dev and readonly in prod. I merged my company kubeconfig but contexts look weird. Who should I ping for RBAC? Thanks!

Sam Patel: @Maria Chen welcome! For dev namespace we can create a ServiceAccount and a RoleBinding. For prod readonly we'll need an approval ticket (security review). Which contexts show up in your kubeconfig?

Maria Chen: I see contexts: "aws-dev", "aws-stage", "redwood-hosted". Not sure which maps to team-platform-dev. I tried `kubectl get ns --context=redwood-hosted` and got 'Unauthorized'.

Sam Patel: Ok run `kubectl config view --minify --context=redwood-hosted` then paste the user name (it's a cert/token). If it's your merged SSO user you'll need to switch to the SA we provision.

Sam Patel: I'll provision a SA called `maria-chen` in team-platform-dev and bind `edit`. It'll take me a few mins.

Eli (infra-bot): ServiceAccount maria-chen created in namespace team-platform-dev. RoleBinding maria-chen-edit -> Role edit applied. Kubeconfig snippet attached via secure link: https://internal.redwood/creds/1994012345

Nate (devex): Quick tip — to add the new context without touching your main kubeconfig run:
```
kubectl config view --flatten > ~/.kube/redwood-maria.yaml
KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/redwood-maria.yaml kubectl config use-context maria-chen@team-platform-dev
```
That keeps your SSO creds separate.

Maria Chen: Thanks! One more: how do I switch to readonly prod later without credentials overlapping?

Sam Patel: For prod readonly we'll give you a different kubeconfig with a read-only SA. Since prod needs approval, open a ticket at https://support.redwood.internal/prod-access and ping @security. Plan ~1 business day. Once approved we'll provide a separate kubeconfig file — same pattern as Nate suggested.

Maria Chen: Got it — I can wait. Appreciate the help :raised_hands: 

Eli (infra-bot): NOTE: The secure kubeconfig link will expire in 24 hours. If you need it reissued, reply here or DM infra.

Maria Chen: Confirmed I can `KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/redwood-maria.yaml kubectl get pods -n team-platform-dev` — looks good. Closing the thread. Thanks all :heart:
